questions.prompt: For a steady tone at the same pitch, what wave property increases as it gets louder?
questions.hint: Picture giving a playground swing a stronger push on each trip, without a faster rhythm.
questions.explanation: At fixed frequency and otherwise comparable conditions, greater sound-pressure amplitude corresponds to greater intensity and ordinarily greater perceived loudness. The reading says the trumpet sound grows louder; it does not specify frequency, waveform, or a physical mechanism for the divine event.
questions.authorFinding: Four real wave properties. Same-pitch condition avoids confusing loudness with frequency. Different sound attribute from accepted Science timbre question. Hint names pressure swings and may closely paraphrase amplitude; evaluate clue value. Post-freeze hint repair: Uses a familiar motion analogy to distinguish strength of oscillation from repetition rate, without naming pressure or restating its definition. Not an exact model of pendulum timing. Test whether the extra analogy helps rather than adding another inference.

questions.prompt: In an engraved intaglio print, where is the ink that forms the lines held?
answers: In grooves cut below the surface
On raised ridges above the surface
questions.hint: Think about the residue left after wiping a scratched cutting board.
questions.explanation: Intaglio engraving holds line-forming ink in incised grooves, which transfer it under pressure to paper. Job wishes for durable written or engraved words. The shared action is cutting into a surface; the passage does not describe printing from a metal plate.
questions.authorFinding: Four real printmaking mechanisms. Distinct from category History relief-printing question, but intentionally related opposite technique; avoid neighboring sessions if repetition becomes noticeable. Hint provides wiping mechanism but is close to the answer. Post-freeze hint repair: Uses a household wiping analogy without naming ink, grooves, cuts or the correct option.
